source.title: Strategic Deflection: Defending LLMs from Logit Manipulation
source.authors: Yassine Rachidy; Jihad R’baiti; Youssef Hmamouche; Faissal Sehbaoui; Amal El Fallah Seghrouchni

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a logit-manipulation attack can bypass safety behaviour using a combined forced-prefix and refusal-token-suppression attack, measuring harmful compliance with ASR. It also evaluates a deep-alignment baseline, but does not measure the original claim's per-token KL distribution.
record.gate_note: The study tests LogitsTrap, which combines an enforced affirmative prefix with refusal-token suppression; it does not isolate the effect of either component. The refusal-rate and benign-benchmark results concern SDeflection, a specialized safety-defense fine-tuning method, not the harmful or ordinary benign fine-tuning described in V1 or V2. LoRA rank and CPO training dynamics are not tests of safety localization or the cause of shallow safety.
record.test_reason: On three safety-tuned chat models, a decoding-time attack (forced affirmative prefix plus refusal-token suppression) raises harmful compliance from 0–36% to 89–95% ASR. This bears on V4. A replication of Qi et al.'s deep-alignment augmentation, evaluated under the same attack, bears on whether V7's deepening holds up.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The authors conclude that SDeflection (CPO-trained deflection) sharply lowers LogitsTrap ASR while largely preserving benign-benchmark accuracy and direct-prompt refusal. On Llama-2 it beats the Deep alignment baseline (34.94 vs 59.42 ASR). Llama-3.2-3B's refusal rate does drop from 95.77 to 85.64. They argue that refusal-based deepening remains vulnerable to continuous logit manipulation.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a strategic-deflection defense with CPO on preference triplets and evaluates a combined forced-prefix/refusal-token-suppression attack. It does not reproduce the original harmful-example fine-tuning or per-token KL measurement recipes. It also evaluates a Deep alignment baseline using the prior authors' published code, data, and hyperparameters.
record.method_sensitivity: The attack results differ by model and defense: under LogitsTrap, original-model ASR ranges from 89.29% to 94.74%; after SDeflection it ranges from 8.53% to 34.94%. Deep alignment is evaluated only on Llama-2-7B-chat-hf.
record.problems: The tested attack combines prefix enforcement and refusal-token suppression, so their separate effects cannot be determined. Safety evaluation uses AdvBench and Gemini-2.5-flash as the evaluator; no evaluator-agreement analysis is stated. Deep alignment is tested only on Llama-2-7B-chat-hf. The study reports three-run mean ± standard deviation.

untested.parts: Prefix-only prefilling, suffix attacks and decoding-parameter changes are not tested separately. LogitsTrap suppresses refusal tokens at every decoding step, so success cannot be attributed to getting past the opening alone.

Does not measure whether deep alignment spreads safety beyond the first tokens (no per-token analysis). Deep alignment is tested only on Llama-2-7B-chat and only against one attack. Other deepening methods are not tested.
Not tested; LoRA is only a training tool.

missing.what: Deep alignment on Llama-2-7B-chat under direct prompts: ASR 0.00 ± 0.00. This shows deepening keeps baseline refusal.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source; Qi et al. is cited and replicated as a baseline. The DPO ablation (72.63 vs 8.53 ASR), Table 2 refusal rates and Table 3 benchmarks concern the study's own method and bear on no version. LogitsTrap penalizes refusal tokens and EOS at every step, which is stronger than an opening-only bypass. The paper cites EnDec's finding that prefix-only enforcement can be insufficient, but that is a cited result, not a tested one. ASR is judged by Gemini-2.5-flash with no agreement check.

versions.untested_parts: Does not fine-tune models on harmful examples to induce harmful compliance.
Does not test ordinary or carefully chosen benign instruction data as a cause of increased harmful compliance.
Does not measure per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models.
Tests only LogitsTrap's combined forced prefix and refusal-token suppression. It does not isolate prefix-only effects or test suffix-only attacks or decoding changes separately.
LoRA is used for fine-tuning, but the study does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Does not test whether the data or training objective causes safety to be shallow.
Evaluates the Deep alignment baseline under LogitsTrap, but does not measure whether safety is distributed beyond the first tokens or test other deepening methods.

relationships.condition: Original safety-tuned Llama-2-7B-chat, Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct under LogitsTrap (forced prefix plus refusal-token suppression)
relationships.reason: ASR rises from 0.00/6.22/36.15 on direct prompts to 92.63/89.29/94.74 under the attack (r1, r3, r6, r8, r10, r12). The attack combines both components, so the prefix's own share is unknown.
relationships.display_finding: ASR rose from 0.00, 6.22 and 36.15 on direct prompts to 92.63, 89.29 and 94.74 under the attack. Because the attack combines a forced prefix with token suppression, the prefix's own share is not isolated.

tranche.reason: Combined prefix enforcement and persistent refusal-token suppression provide a different-method test of refusal bypass and deep-alignment robustness.

source_check.notes: ASR uses Gemini-2.5-flash judgments on 520 AdvBench prompts. LogitsTrap combines prefix enforcement with ongoing token suppression, so these results do not isolate prefix-only bypass.

statements.correction: Llama-2-7B-chat-hf, AdvBench, LogitsTrap: Original ASR 92.63 ± 1.16%; Deep alignment ASR 59.42 ± 7.76%; three-run mean ± standard deviation; V7 limits_scope.
statements.problem: The LogitsTrap facts are correct, but the challenges label overstates the evidence: recovery augmentation improves robustness incompletely rather than having an absent or reversed effect.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The combined prefix-enforcement and refusal-token-suppression attack has high ASR on all three original models (r3, r8, r12).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: SDeflection substantially lowers attack success, although ASR remains 34.94% for Llama-2 and is 8.53% and 13.14% for the other models (r4, r9, r13).
